sourceRun.label: Primary release evidence review
sourceRun.method: Agent review of canonical release timestamps, published roadmap, complete governance histories and operator deployment receipts

candidates.label: Tezos X Mainnet
candidates.summary: Etherlink kernel 7.1 has a completed mainnet deployment receipt. The official Tezos X roadmap still labels Q3 activation planned; the broader launch remains unconfirmed in this review.
candidates.nextSignal: Explicit full Tezos X rollout declaration tied to the deployed kernel and operator compatibility
candidates.highlight: Ganesha introduced the Michelson/NAC infrastructure proposal. Confirmed kernel deployment and the broader Tezos X rollout remain separate claims.

gates.label: Runtime hardening
gates.detail: Ganesha describes the Michelson interface and native atomic composability; kernel deployment does not establish completion of the wider Tezos X roadmap.

gates.label: Previewnet stability
gates.detail: The official Previewnet and documentation remain available for testing. A public test environment is not a production-readiness certificate.

gates.label: Node and tooling compatibility
gates.detail: EVM node 0.65 is published. Ganesha required at least 0.64 and a restart to expose Michelson RPCs after activation; each operator remains responsible for compatibility.

gates.label: Mainnet proposal readiness
gates.detail: Ganesha was publicly proposed for the SLOW track. The reviewed archive contains SLOW proposal 40 and promotion 41; the old no-public-proposal claim is retracted.

gates.label: Etherlink governance
gates.detail: FAST periods 636/637 record the kernel 7.1 proposal and promotion. SLOW and FAST outcomes remain distinct; an empty current window cannot erase historical governance.

gates.label: Production rollout
gates.detail: Etherlink reports kernel 7.1 mainnet maintenance completed August 29. Its deployment is confirmed; a separate declaration of the full Tezos X rollout is still required.

evidence.label: Current official Tezos X roadmap
evidence.note: The page labels mainnet activation Q3 2026 and Planned. This is a published target, not an independently confirmed full-rollout date.

evidence.label: Ganesha proposal and scope
evidence.note: The July 31 post describes Michelson/NAC infrastructure, a SLOW-track proposal, the 0.64 operator minimum and a separate later full Tezos X rollout.

evidence.label: Complete official SLOW period archive
evidence.note: SLOW 40/41 record the August proposal and promotion. Period 41 has Nay-dominant voting power; its result must not be conflated with later FAST votes.

evidence.label: Complete official FAST period archive
evidence.note: FAST 636/637 record proposal 00db5a8b279b9915f7ffef420347b5d9667ac4e73a9c766b7ef71513f748f52c67 and August 28 promotion. Current-window absence is not historical absence.

evidence.label: Etherlink 7.1 mainnet deployment
evidence.note: Official maintenance names kernel 7.1 mainnet activation, beginning August 29 at 19:45:14 UTC and ending at 20:45:14 UTC. This is an operator deployment receipt.

evidence.label: Tezos X documentation scope
evidence.note: Documentation still describes an experimental testnet. This lag relative to kernel deployment is exposed as a source discrepancy, not resolved by inventing a full launch.

evidence.label: EVM node 0.65 release receipt
evidence.note: The canonical release record identifies version 0.65 and released_at 2026-08-24T17:07:09.170Z; source commit time is a separate clock.

history.reason: EVM node 0.64 shipped and advanced tooling compatibility; confidence did not rise because the public mainnet proposal is still absent.
Previewnet kernel 0.8 shipped, but the reviewed FAST governance window still has no winning mainnet-kernel candidate.
Kernel 0.9 was cut on master and the Previewnet installer was corrected, but the reviewed FAST governance window still has no winning mainnet-kernel candidate.

Retracted the earlier FAST-null inference after reviewing SLOW/FAST histories and the 7.1 deployment. Q3 remains an official target; conflicting rollout documentation lowers confidence in the full-launch forecast.

September 8 re-review: canonical release records and complete SLOW/FAST histories are unchanged; the completed kernel 7.1 deployment remains distinct from the roadmap target and experimental-testnet documentation. No new full-rollout declaration was confirmed in these reviewed sources.

candidates.label: Octez 25.2
candidates.summary: Octez 25.2 is published with binaries on the canonical release page. Its GitLab release record dates publication to September 2; the August 24 source-commit date is not the release date.
candidates.nextSignal: A separately published next Octez release or release candidate
candidates.highlight: Published binaries and the canonical tag replace the old backport-only forecast.

evidence.label: Canonical Octez releases and binaries
evidence.note: The official page identifies Octez 25.2 as latest and exposes x86_64 and arm64 binaries with SHA-256 checksums.

evidence.label: Octez 25.2 protected tag
evidence.note: Protected tag at f606285304de0294926946b8b474a1e38a5b5972. The tag page shows the source commit date; the release record supplies publication time.

evidence.label: Octez 25.2 publication timestamp
evidence.note: released_at is 2026-09-02T14:22:03.407Z and upcoming_release is false. The deprecated GitLab page points users to octez.tezos.com/releases/.

history.reason: A merge request named for 25.2 opened against the v25 release branch, creating the first credible near-term signal.
The DAL backport train merged successfully, but no version bump, package, candidate, or 25.2 tag is published yet.
Canonical binaries, the protected tag and a September 2 release record confirm 25.2 shipped. The earlier backport-only forecast is superseded.
September 8 re-review confirmed the same published operator release against its canonical tag list, release record, and downloadable artifacts. Publication time and release scope are unchanged.

candidates.label: EVM Node 0.65
candidates.summary: EVM node 0.65 is the latest protected EVM-node tag in the reviewed canonical list, with a published release and static binaries. It is separate from the Tezos X full-rollout decision.
candidates.nextSignal: A separately published next EVM-node tag or release candidate
candidates.highlight: 0.65 supersedes the previous 0.64 release receipt; operator release publication does not certify the full Tezos X launch.

evidence.label: Canonical protected release tags
evidence.note: The reviewed list identifies octez-evm-node-v0.65 as the latest protected EVM-node tag, at commit 0ee84d6b.

evidence.label: EVM node 0.65 release and publication
evidence.note: The canonical record supplies released_at 2026-08-24T17:07:09.170Z, upcoming_release false and a static-binaries package link.

history.reason: Direct release preparation and an explicit Previewnet dependency produced a high-confidence days horizon.
The canonical protected tag replaced the forecast with a confirmed release.
Version 0.65 has a canonical August 24 publication record and static binaries. It supersedes 0.64; draft work is no longer used as the release-status proxy.
September 8 re-review confirmed the same published operator release against its canonical tag list, release record, and downloadable artifacts. Publication time and release scope are unchanged.

methodology: Octez, the EVM node, Tezos X Previewnet, kernel governance, kernel deployment and the full Tezos X rollout remain separate claims.
Confidence comes from direct artifacts and coordinated evidence, never raw merge volume or a completion percentage.
Q3 2026 is the current official roadmap target, not a confirmed full-rollout date. Deployed kernel infrastructure does not settle contradictory platform documentation.
Governance review checks complete SLOW and FAST histories. An empty current FAST window cannot prove that no public proposal or governance vote has ever existed.
releasedAt uses the canonical release record publication clock, never a source commit timestamp. Review timestamps describe this review and do not refresh upstream facts.
The browser renders reviewed evidence, marks the receipt stale after 36 hours and removes it at expiry. Extending those clocks requires another substantive source review.
